clue.text: Jump through or skip

parts.note: to jump is to hop
per means through or by means of, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: An instruction to leap through something, or else skip it.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip and a hopper are both big open-topped containers for loading and tipping material.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are open bins used to hold and discharge loose material such as rubble or grain.

clue.text: Get lost in the saying of hum and haw, for example?

definitions.text: Get lost in the saying of hum and haw, for example?

parts.words: Get lost in the saying of hum and haw, for example?
parts.note: to lose one's words mid-speech, making noises like um and er while one dithers

explanation.surface: Losing one's way while uttering filler noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithering, pausing and uttering fillers is wavering before acting or speaking.

clue.text: Individual in post of colonizer

indicators.note: the word for individual is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a pier is a pillar or post supporting a structure
an individual is one

explanation.surface: A single person posted out to govern a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler who goes first into new territory is a founding settler.

clue.text: Bride more disposed to decorate? -

indicators.note: the letters are arranged, or disposed, in a different way

explanation.surface: A bride keener on adorning things than most.
explanation.definitionFit: To ornament with needlework, or embellish a story, is to decorate it.

clue.text: Hants map spread out in the shade

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A map of Hampshire (Hants) unfolded in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Hants is the usual abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county; 'spread out' rearranges HANTS MAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a ghost or apparition, an illusory spectre.

clue.text: Fluid studies of spa-resort technicians?

parts.note: a hydro is a spa hotel offering water treatments
mechanics are technicians who repair machines

explanation.surface: What engineers working at a spa might study.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of how liquids move and act under force is the study of fluids.

clue.text: Christened me Dan by mistake

indicators.note: the letters are muddled up, as if written wrongly

explanation.surface: A complaint that a baby was baptised with the wrong name.
explanation.definitionFit: Being christened is being given a name at baptism.

clue.text: Branches of royal family, velvet-clad when young

definitions.text: Branches of royal family, velvet-clad when young

parts.words: Branches of royal family, velvet-clad when young
parts.note: sounds like royal lineage, but a royal is a stag with twelve points, whose branching horns are covered in soft velvet while growing

explanation.surface: Young members of a royal house dressed in velvet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag's branched horns grow covered in soft skin called velvet.

clue.text: Musicians' gallery to undergo change

parts.note: MU is the Musicians' Union
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A minstrels' gallery about to be refurbished.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a London art gallery; MU is the British Musicians' Union.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter in form or nature is to transform or change.

clue.text: Badly insulted fat man, a back-to-basics sort

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are jumbled, done badly

explanation.surface: A fat man was rudely insulted by a traditionalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict adherent of core doctrines wants a return to first principles.

clue.text: Unable to move after a fall outside?

definitions.text: Unable to move after a fall outside?

parts.words: Unable to move after a fall outside?
parts.note: reads like someone injured by tumbling outdoors, but the fall is of flakes from the sky, trapping people indoors

explanation.surface: Someone who has slipped outdoors and cannot get up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being trapped by heavy drifts after a winter storm is being cut off by settled flakes.

clue.text: Assembled to introduce old books of choral music

indicators.note: the word for assembled takes the other piece into its middle

parts.note: people who assembled met
OT is the Old Testament, the old books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A gathering held to present antique volumes of choir pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A short polyphonic sacred piece for unaccompanied voices is a kind of choral composition.

clue.text: Mountaineer's first purchase?

parts.note: looks like the first item a climber buys, but purchase means grip: the first small grip a foot finds on rock

explanation.surface: What a new climber buys first in a gear shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ledge giving a foot its first grip is a climber's initial hold or foothold.

clue.text: Scrap unmatched pieces before end of tournament

parts.note: an odd sock is unmatched
chessmen are pieces, so pieces are men

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word tournament is used

explanation.surface: A fight between ill-matched chess pieces just before a tournament ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight, but here it is a leftover bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover fragment or remnant is a stray bit of material.

clue.text: Drained portion of spaghetti reheated

indicators.note: only a run of letters within the words spaghetti reheated is taken

explanation.surface: Warmed-up pasta poured into a colander.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the run across the words is TIREH, not the answer; the setter or printer slipped one letter, and the hidden run is meant to end in D.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling drained means being exhausted and worn out.

clue.text: Patience of people keen to order in dining-room?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for the dining room

parts.note: a mess is a dining room for service personnel

indicators.note: the letters of keen are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Asking about the forbearance of diners eager to order a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to order' looks like asking for food in a restaurant; it is the anagram signal, and a mess is the shared dining room of a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience and mild submissiveness are both a quiet, uncomplaining humility.

clue.text: Irritated about a road that is short, though it is close

indicators.note: the word for irritated goes around the other pieces

parts.note: niggly means irritable or irritated
RD is the short form of road

explanation.surface: Annoyed by a short road, though it is near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like near, but it means stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Close in the old sense means mean with money, stingy.

clue.text: One should not allow butters to go off

definitions.text: One should not allow butters to go off

parts.words: One should not allow butters to go off
parts.note: sounds like a dairy rule against butter turning rancid, but butters are animals that butt, which a herdsman keeps from straying

explanation.surface: Advice to a dairy worker about keeping butter fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A herdsman of billies and nannies keeps the butting beasts from wandering.

clue.text: A bloomer in a marathon, perhaps, having no oxygen!

indicators.note: the remaining letters are offered as one possible arrangement of themselves
a letter is removed from the words a marathon

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A runner makes a blunder mid-race, gasping for air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' removes O from A MARATHON to leave AMARATHN, which 'perhaps' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer here is a flowering plant, and love-lies-bleeding is one such flower.

clue.text: Gemstone cut for a nobleman

indicators.note: the word for the gem is trimmed of its last letter

parts.note: a marquise is a gemstone with a pointed oval cut

explanation.surface: A jewel cut specially for an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank of nobility between an earl and a duke.

clue.text: Blow ring in enjoyment

parts.note: a gust is a blow of wind
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Blowing a smoke ring with relish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty relish or zest is keen enjoyment.

clue.text: "Ambition should be made of — stuff" (/ Caesar)

definitions.text: "Ambition should be made of — stuff" (/ Caesar)

parts.words: "Ambition should be made of — stuff" (/ Caesar)
parts.note: a quotation from Shakespeare's Julius Caesar with the missing word to be supplied; the slash is the J of the play's title misread

explanation.surface: Mark Antony's line about ambition in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Antony's speech means harder or more severe.

clue.text: Crazy, irrational number following a sailor

indicators.note: the number comes after the sailor

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
a surd is an irrational root number

explanation.surface: A sailor doing wild maths with irrational numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridiculous and unreasonable means wildly foolish.

clue.text: Capital investment for father

parts.note: sounds like money a dad puts into a business, but capital means of the head: headwear a priest invests in

explanation.surface: Dad putting money into a business venture.
explanation.definitionFit: A square cap worn by Catholic clergy is head-gear for a priest, addressed as Father.

clue.text: A. Trollope, we hear, put up here in America

indicators.note: in a down entry the letters are read upwards, reversing them

parts.note: taken as written
the novelist's name sounds like trollop, a slatternly woman, so slut

explanation.surface: Anthony Trollope, it is said, stayed somewhere in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: TULSA is a city in Oklahoma; 'we hear' makes Trollope sound like trollop.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Oklahoma is a place in the United States.

clue.text: Hearing organ in resort can be most intimate

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a nest is a snug retreat or haunt
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A medical note about an ear at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' tempts as an anagram signal, but it is a retreat, NEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Closest in relationship means dearest and most intimate.

clue.text: Samuel's fourth letter to Saul possibly expected?

indicators.note: the letter in fourth place of the name Samuel is taken
the name Saul could be spelt in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A biblical letter from Samuel to Saul, perhaps anticipated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something customary is what one would normally anticipate.

clue.text: Frequency with which firm is dropped from correspondence

indicators.note: the abbreviation for a firm is removed from the longer word

parts.note: a coincidence is a correspondence or agreement of things
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: How often a company is struck off a mailing list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' looks like letters but means agreement, COINCIDENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidence is the rate of occurrence, how often something happens.

clue.text: Independent airs up on the pitch?

definitions.text: Independent airs up on the pitch?

parts.words: Independent airs up on the pitch?
parts.note: sounds like free-roaming broadcasts at a sports ground, but means separate melodies sung higher in pitch above a tune

explanation.surface: Freelance broadcasts made at a football ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Counter-melodies sung above the main tune are separate airs at a higher register.

clue.text: Henry approaching lines I would cross

parts.note: Hy is an old abbreviation for the name Henry
BR is British Rail, a network of railway lines
I'd is the short form of I would

explanation.surface: Henry nears some lines that he means to step across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a mongrel or crossbreed.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbreed is an offspring of two different varieties.
